title: Customer self-create rule does not constrain spinsRemaining — a first-time customer can grant themselves unlimited bonus spins (wallet cashback + coupons)
detail: The `customers/{userId}` create rule (firestore.rules:188-194) is the production path for profile creation — both clients write the doc themselves after sign-in (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:97 `setDoc(ref, defaultCustomer(...))`, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:306 `ref.set(_defaultCustomer(...))`). The rule validates only five fields: uid, role=='customer', isBlocked==false, profileComplete==false, affiliate==null and wallet.balancePaise==0. Every other field on the payload is accepted verbatim, including `spinsRemaining` and the whole `stats` map. There is no Firestore trigger anywhere in functions/src (no onDocumentCreated/onDocumentWritten exists in the codebase) that normalises a newly created customer doc. `spinsRemaining` is the admin-granted bonus-spin balance: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:134 lets a spin through when `usedPre >= spinsPerDay` as long as `spinsRemaining > 0`, the transaction re-checks the same value at line 147-150, and line 169 only decrements it by 1 per spin. A cashback slice credits real wallet money at execute.ts:173-176 (`wallet.balancePaise` increment), and wallet balance is spendable at checkout (walletUsedPaise in orders/checkout.ts). The customers UPDATE rule (firestore.rules:179-184) correctly excludes spinsRemaining, so the field is only forgeable at create time — but create happens exactly once per account, under the attacker's control, on their very first sign-in.
failure_scenario: Attacker completes a genuine MSG91 OTP sign-in with their own phone (verifyOtp returns a custom token; no customers/{uid} doc exists yet). Instead of letting the app create the doc, they call the Firestore REST/JS API themselves: setDoc('customers/<their uid>', {uid, role:'customer', isBlocked:false, profileComplete:false, affiliate:null, wallet:{balancePaise:0,...}, spinsRemaining: 1000000, stats:{ordersCount: 99, ...}}). The rule accepts it. They then call executeSpin repeatedly against the live campaign: the daily cap (spinsPerDay) is exhausted after the first spins, after which every further spin is paid for out of the forged spinsRemaining balance, decrementing 1 at a time from 1,000,000. Each cashback slice increments wallet.balancePaise by slice.discountValuePaise, and each discount slice mints a fresh customers/{uid}/coupons doc. The forged stats.ordersCount also passes the 'existing customers only' campaign eligibility check at execute.ts:100-107. Result: unbounded wallet credit and unbounded coupon minting from a brand-new account.
fix: Add the remaining privileged fields to the create rule: `request.resource.data.spinsRemaining == 0`, `request.resource.data.referredBy == null`, `request.resource.data.stats.ordersCount == 0 && request.resource.data.stats.totalSpentPaise == 0`, and `request.resource.data.wallet.lifetimeCreditsPaise == 0 && request.resource.data.wallet.breakdown.cashbackPaise == 0` (etc). Better, do what the comment at firestore.rules:186-187 already prescribes: set create back to `if false` and have verifyOtp (which already knows the uid and the verified phone) create the doc with the Admin SDK before returning the custom token, so the shape is server-owned on both clients.

title: resolveUid keys identity on an unverified email address that any client can claim, so a pre-created account hijacks the phone number's uid
detail: resolveUid (otp.ts:203-228) resolves the Firebase uid for a verified phone by looking up `otp_<digits>@mock.barakath.app` FIRST (line 209) and returning that account's uid, before it ever tries getUserByPhoneNumber (line 221). The email is fully derivable from the phone number (line 47). Email/Password sign-up is an enabled, publicly callable provider on this project: the admin panel signs in with it (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:23), createSubAdmin creates password users (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:49), and the deliberately retained mock OTP fallback creates accounts straight from a browser with the public web API key (web/src/lib/otp/mockOtpService.ts:132 `createUserWithEmailAndPassword`). Nothing in resolveUid checks that the found account was created before the MSG91 cut-over, that it has no password provider, or that its phoneNumber was already the one being verified — line 210-214 does the opposite: it force-attaches the verified phone number to whatever account owns that email, swallowing the failure. The returned uid is then handed a custom token (line 269) and is the uid every order, wallet balance, address and wishlist item hangs off.
failure_scenario: Attacker knows a target's mobile number 9876543210 (or simply enumerates numbers). Before the target ever signs in, the attacker calls the public Identity Toolkit signUp endpoint with the project's web API key (present in web/.env.local and in the APK) using email `otp_919876543210@mock.barakath.app` and a password only they know. Later the target signs in for real: sendOtp/verifyOtp succeed, resolveUid's getUserByEmail hits the attacker's account, line 213 attaches +919876543210 to it, and verifyOtp mints a custom token for the ATTACKER'S uid. The target now transacts on an account whose password the attacker holds — the attacker signs in with signInWithEmailAndPassword at any time and reads/writes the victim's customers doc, order history, addresses and wallet, with no OTP, no attempt cap and no MSG91 involvement. Reversing the two lookups is not sufficient on its own: with a squatted email and no legacy account, createUser at line 226 then fails with email-already-exists and the victim cannot sign in at all.
fix: Stop treating the mock email as an identity key for anything but genuine legacy accounts: look up getUserByPhoneNumber first, and only fall back to the legacy email when `user.metadata.creationTime` predates the MSG91 cut-over date AND the account has no other phone attached; when reusing it, strip the password credential (auth.updateUser(uid,{password: undefined}) is not supported, so use updateUser to a random secret or delete the password provider) so the legacy credential cannot be replayed. On the console side, disable client-side email/password sign-up for this project (Identity Platform → sign-up quota / blocking function) now that admin accounts are only ever created by createSubAdmin, and create the account with a random email on line 226 instead of the derivable one.

title: sendOtp per-number rate limit is a non-atomic read-then-write — N parallel calls all pass the 5-per-hour cap
detail: sendOtp counts existing session docs for the phone (recentSendCount, otp.ts:104-113) and compares to MAX_SENDS_PER_WINDOW at line 120, but the session doc that makes the count go up is only written at line 131, after the MSG91 round-trip. The check and the write are not in a transaction and there is no per-phone lock document, unlike verifyOtp, which explicitly uses db.runTransaction (line 241-252) for exactly this reason. The callable is unauthenticated by design (it must be, it precedes sign-in) and App Check is off, so any client can fire an unlimited number of concurrent requests, all of which observe the same pre-write count.
failure_scenario: An attacker POSTs 200 concurrent sendOtp calls with {phone:'919876543210'}. Every one of them runs recentSendCount before any of them has written its session doc, so all 200 read a count of 0 (or the same stale value) and all 200 pass the >=5 gate. 200 real SMS are sent to the victim's handset and billed to the MSG91 account; the hourly ceiling is only enforced against the requests that arrive after the writes land. Repeating this every hour, or against many numbers at once (nothing caps distinct numbers per caller), turns the callable into a free SMS-bombing endpoint at the owner's cost.
fix: Move the counter into a transaction on a per-phone document (e.g. `otpRateLimits/{phone}` holding {windowStartedAt, count}); read+increment inside db.runTransaction BEFORE calling MSG91, and roll the count back (or leave it, failing closed) if the MSG91 send throws. That also removes the count() aggregation query from the hot path.

title: resendOtp resend budget and 30s cooldown are non-atomic — parallel resends bypass both
detail: resendOtp reads the session (loadSession, line 171), checks `resends >= MAX_RESENDS` (line 174) and `Date.now() - lastSentAt < RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS` (line 179-185) against that snapshot, calls MSG91 (line 187), and only then writes `resends: resends + 1, lastSentAt: now` (line 188). Nothing is transactional. The comment at line 177-178 states the intent — 'a client can always be bypassed, and each resend costs a real SMS' — but the server-side enforcement is defeated by the same trick it was written to stop. verifyOtp in the same file gets this right with an explicit transaction (line 241-252), so the omission is inconsistent within the file itself.
failure_scenario: Client obtains a session from sendOtp, then fires 20 concurrent resendOtp calls with the same sessionId. All 20 read resends=0 and the same lastSentAt, so all 20 pass both the 3-resend cap and the 30-second cooldown; MSG91 sends 20 SMS and the final write leaves `resends: 1`, so the client can repeat the burst indefinitely without ever exhausting the budget. The per-number hourly ceiling does not stop this either — resends do not create session docs, so recentSendCount never sees them.
fix: Wrap the whole load/validate/increment in db.runTransaction on the session ref (claim the resend slot and stamp lastSentAt before the MSG91 call), exactly as verifyOtp claims an attempt.

title: A sign-in whose customers/{uid} write fails leaves the account permanently unusable — create-profile only ever UPDATEs the doc
detail: The customer doc is created client-side and only inside the OTP verify path: app/lib/features/auth/otp_screen.dart:137 (`repo.ensureCustomerDoc(e164)`) and web/src/components/auth/authActions.ts:175. Both run AFTER the Firebase session has been established (signInWithCustomToken already succeeded and the server has burned the OTP session with verified:true at otp.ts:258). If that single Firestore write fails — transient offline, the app being backgrounded, a rules hiccup — the user keeps a persisted Firebase session with no customers doc, and there is no second creation path anywhere in either client (grep for ensureCustomerDoc returns only those two call sites). Recovery is impossible from the screen the user is then routed to: the app's completeProfile does `ref.update({...})` (auth_repository.dart:360) and the web's completeCustomerProfile does `updateDoc(...)` (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:107); an update against a non-existent document fails (and cannot satisfy the rules' onlyFields diff against a null resource). Retrying the OTP is no help either: the session is already verified, so verifyOtp answers failed-precondition 'This code has already been used.' (otp.ts:159-161).
failure_scenario: User verifies the OTP on the app in a lift; signInWithCustomToken succeeds, then ensureCustomerDoc's write fails on the dropped connection. The generic catch at otp_screen.dart:157-163 toasts "Couldn't verify the code" and the user stays on the OTP screen — but they ARE signed in. They kill the app and relaunch: splash_screen.dart:53 sees an authenticated user, isProfileComplete() returns false (no doc), and routes to Create Profile. Tapping 'Enter Barakath' calls completeProfile → update on a missing doc → NOT_FOUND/permission-denied → 'Could not save your profile. Please try again.' forever. Tapping Skip drops them on Home with no customer doc, where cart writes, address writes and wishlist counters all fail silently. The same dead end exists on web (/create-profile → completeProfile → updateDoc). The only escape is to find and use Log out, then sign in again and spend another OTP.
fix: Make the profile write self-healing: use set(..., merge/SetOptions(merge:true)) with the default document when the doc is missing (both clients), or, preferably, create customers/{uid} server-side inside verifyOtp before the custom token is returned, so the doc's existence is guaranteed by the same call that establishes the session.

title: firestore.rules isSuperAdmin() trusts the ID-token claim alone, so a demoted or suspended super admin keeps reading auditLogs and complianceLogs for up to an hour
detail: `can()` (rules:39-44) was deliberately hardened to re-read admins/{uid} and require status=='active', with the comment at rules:34-38 stating that a claim 'lives in an ID token for up to an hour, so a claim-only check kept a suspended or demoted admin fully privileged until their token expired' and that 'every gate below does the same'. isSuperAdmin() (rules:22) does not: it is `isSignedIn() && role() == 'super_admin'`, purely the custom claim, and it gates the reads on complianceLogs (rules:293) and auditLogs (rules:296) — the money/actor audit trail. Neither revoking refresh tokens (subAdmins.ts:112, 138) nor disabling the Auth user (subAdmins.ts:137) invalidates an already-issued ID token for Firestore Security Rules; revocation is only honoured by verifyIdToken(checkRevoked) on the server, which rules do not perform. The functions-side equivalent, requireSuperAdmin (functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:75-82), does re-read the stored doc, so this is rules-only drift.
failure_scenario: Super admin A is demoted to sub_admin (or suspended) at 10:00. updateSubAdmin sets the new claims and revokes A's refresh tokens, and the admin panel's doc watcher signs A out of the UI (authStore.ts:57-60). A, expecting this, has kept the ID token issued at 09:59 (copied from devtools, or simply keeps an open tab that has not refreshed). Until 10:59 that token still carries role:'super_admin', so a direct Firestore REST/SDK read of `auditLogs` and `complianceLogs` succeeds — the full record of who moved which customer's money, refund amounts, block reasons and admin actor names — after the account was supposed to be locked out.
fix: Define isSuperAdmin() the same way can() is defined: `isAdmin() && adminDoc().status == 'active' && adminDoc().role == 'super_admin'` so the stored admins doc is authoritative for the audit-log collections too.

title: Any signed-in user can squat an arbitrary phone key in the pre-auth users directory
detail: `match /users/{phoneKey}` allows create for any signed-in user as long as the payload's uid is their own — the document ID (the phone number) is never checked against the caller's verified phone (rules:227-232). The collection is the pre-auth existence gate the web sign-in/register screens branch on (web/src/lib/userDirectory.ts:29, web/src/components/auth/authActions.ts:106-107) and it is publicly readable per-document (`allow get: if true`), so a phone number can be tested for existence by anyone and claimed by anyone with a session.
failure_scenario: A user signs in legitimately, then writes users/919876543210 (a number they do not own) with {phone:'+919876543210', uid:<their own uid>, createdAt}. The rule accepts it and, since update/delete are denied, the entry can never be corrected. When the real owner of that number goes to /register on web, requestOtp('signup') sees userExists==true and refuses with 'already_registered'. Scripted over a range of numbers this makes web registration unusable for those customers (they can still get in via /signin, which passes the same gate, so no account is taken over — the damage is a permanently wrong, unremovable directory entry and a blocked registration path).
fix: Require the document id to match the caller's verified phone: `allow create: if isSignedIn() && request.resource.data.uid == uid() && phoneKey == request.auth.token.phone_number.replace('+','')` (the custom token minted by verifyOtp already carries a `phone` claim — otp.ts:269 — so it can be asserted directly), or move the directory write into verifyOtp server-side and deny client writes entirely.
